small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_N×BLOCK_OC tiles (e.g. 256×64, 128×128 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) and prune the obviously bad small tiles; the 128×128×72 GEMM-K is large enough to benefit from bigger N tiles since OH*OW=15876 per batch.
- Replace the per-(kh,kw,ic) scalar broadcast accumulate with a tl.dot: pack the IC*KH*KW=72 reduction into a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]×[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC] matmul (BLOCK_K=72 fits as constexpr) so the kernel uses tensor cores instead of FMA broadcasts — this is the single biggest speedup lever within the current structure.
- Swizzle the program-id mapping (group pid_n in chunks before pid_oc) for better L2 reuse of the weight tile across spatial tiles.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-GEMM with tl.dot: one program per (N tile, OC tile), inner loop over K=IC*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=32 or 72, gathering input via computed offsets (implicit im2col). Fuse bias + hardswish*relu in the epilogue on the accumulator before the store.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout for both input and output so the K dimension (IC) is the contiguous fastest axis — this turns the gather into coalesced loads across BLOCK_K and lets tl.dot run at full tensor-core throughput.
- Pre-pack the weight to (OC, KH*KW*IC) layout once in __init__ (still doing the full conv at runtime — this is just a layout transform, not an algebraic shortcut), so the K-loop reads contiguous weight rows.
